Download go artifacts

Download a module version from a Go proxy (GOPROXY) repository. Without --version
rp finds the latest version the way the go command does: it reads
&lt;repo&gt;/&lt;module&gt;/@v/list (the highest release, else the highest tagged
pre-release, else the highest pseudo-version) and, when that list is empty,
&lt;repo&gt;/&lt;module&gt;/@latest. Then it downloads the three files of the version, each
with a request of its own: .info, .mod and .zip. Upper case letters of the
module path are escaped as the proxy protocol says (BurntSushi becomes
!burnt!sushi in the URL).

The files are stored as &lt;module path with / as _&gt;-&lt;version&gt;.info, .mod and .zip
(a long path is cut from the left). The proxy publishes no checksum (there is no
checksum database), so none of them can be verified against a digest; rp checks
instead that the .info names the requested version, that the .mod declares the
module path, and that the .zip is a zip whose entries all lie under &lt;module&gt;@&lt;version&gt;/, and reports
the files as not verified. Nothing is stored unless all three pass.

```
rp download go <module-path> [flags]
```

## Options

```
      --dir string       Directory to store the file in (created when missing) (default ".")
      --force            Replace the file when it already exists
      --repo string      Repository to download from (required)
      --version string   Version to download (default: the newest the format knows)
```
